praeostendo , endi, ensum, 3, v. a.,
I.to show beforehand, display before, make clear (late. Lat.): hoc monstrare debent, hoc ostendere vel praeostendere, Aug. Civ. Dei, 21, 8, 6.— Absol. : portenta a portendendo, id est, praeostendendo, Aug. Civ. Dei, 21, 8, 6; cf. Isid. 11, 3, 3.—Hence, praeosten-sus , a, um, Part., foreshown (eccl. Lat.): “sabbatum praeostensum et praedictum,” Tert. adv. Jud. 4 : “sacrificia,” id. ib. 5 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
